chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Khalaf, from Mūsā ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bazawfarī, from Abī al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning two horsemen who collided, and one of them died; so he held the surviving one liable for the blood-money of the deceased.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in his capacity as the rightful judicial authority
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money; legally mandated compensation for a death
key_terms.فَضَمَّنَ: he held liable or imposed compensation upon

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام when two horsemen collided and one of them died?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a fatal collision between two horsemen. It establishes liability for the surviving party to pay the diyah of the one who died, reflecting principles of judicial ruling and compensation in cases of harm.
